newsitem.title: GERMANY: FOCUS-Vereinsbank sees 97 profit up over 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Vereinsbank sees 97 profit up over 10 pct.

text.p: Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, Germany's fourth largest bank, plans to increase operating profit by more than 10 percent in 1997 after first-quarter earnings rose 18.7 percent, the bank said on Wednesday.

The bank, whose share price has surged in recent months amid speculation it may be a takeover target, said operating profit before risk provisions rose to 614.7 million marks ($356.6 million) in the first quarter from 517.7 million in the year-ago period.
Earnings in the period were buoyed by a 96.6 percent jump in own-account trading profit to 98.0 million marks while net commission income rose 17.4 percent to 351.7 million marks.
"We're above plan and want to continue the momentum of the first quarter," chief executive Albrecht Schmidt told the bank's annual shareholder meeting.
"We have set a goal of achieving a double-digit (percentage) rise in operating profit after risk provisions for 1997 as well."
In 1996, operating profit after risk provisions by 18.4 percent to 1.636 billion marks.

Analysts said the first-quarter results were within expectations and said the shares were underpinned by takeover speculation after Deutsche Bank AG's announcement last year that it had a 5.21 percent stake in Vereinsbank.

"Vereinsbank's shares are expensive from a fundamental point of view but I'm keeping my 'hold' recommendation for the stock because not much was said today to dampen the takeover speculation," said Markus Strigl, banking analyst at Trinkaus & Burkhardt in Frankfurt.
Vereinsbank's Schmidt told shareholders Germany's banks would not be able to avoid a trend towards consolidation and that his bank would play an important role in that process.
He conceded that the sharp rise in Vereinsbank's share price was explained not only by earnings growth but also by "assumptions about possible structural changes in the German banking market".
The shares were up one mark or 1.3 percent at 74 marks at 1020 GMT while the overall market was lower.
They have risen about 70 percent since July last year when Deutsche announced its stake in a move which fanned merger speculation across Germany's overcrowded banking sector.

Outlining the first-quarter results, Vereinsbank said group net interest income rose 5.3 percent to 1.2 billion marks, mainly resulting from its mortgage lending business which enjoyed strong volume growth.

The bank said it almost matched the extraordinarily strong new mortgage business seen in the first quarter of 1996, with new loan approvals in the first three months of 1997 reaching 12.7 billion marks, down just 3.1 percent year-on-year.
The group lending volume rose by 1.6 percent to 317.4 billion marks, while the group balance sheet total rose by 1.5 percent to 409.6 billion marks.
Schmidt also announced plans to shed a net 800 jobs in Germany in the next one-and-a-half years in a streamlining of its administrative staff.

A spokesman for the bank said Vereinsbank had the potential to shed 1,600 jobs through rationalisation and restructuring but that the bank planned to hire 800 sales staff. Vereinsbank employed 21,825 people at the end of 1996 of whom about 20,000 were in Germany.

Schmidt also said Vereinsbank plans to raise its return on equity after tax to 11 percent in 1998 from 8.6 percent in 1996 and to reduce its cost-income ratio below 60 percent in the next two years from the 1996 level of 62.4 percent.

The bank is aiming to strengthen its position in the market for real estate finance and planned to increase its share of the market for private residential construction finance to 15 percent from six percent.
-- Frankfurt Newsroom, +49 69 756525 ($ = 1.723 German Marks)
